I am 63 years old, and these bones have worked this land for 35 years. My family has eight mouths, and while some of my children send money back from factory jobs in the city, I cannot rely on that forever. I have 30 mu total, and I know every corner of it. My well gives me water when the rains fail, which they often do on this plain.

This year, I will stick to what I know. Twenty mu will go to my wheat-maize rotation — that is the backbone. The wheat is already in the ground from last autumn; I planted an improved variety that has done well here before. I will top-dress it with urea and compound fertilizer in the spring, irrigate it three times at the critical stages, and spray twice for weeds and diseases. I expect about 900 jin per mu. Come June, right after wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid maize immediately. The window is narrow — only a few weeks — so I will use no-tillage planting to save time and labor. I will fertilize the maize, irrigate twice, and spray twice. It should give me about 1,060 jin per mu.

For the other ten mu, I keep five mu of cotton and five mu of garlic. Cotton pays all right, but the picking is hard on my hands and back at my age, so I will not plant more. I will rotary till the cotton field in spring, plant an improved variety, apply fertilizer, irrigate three times, and spray four times for the bollworms that always come. I hope for about 210 jin of lint per mu. The garlic I will plant in spring on five mu — it is heavy work but brings good cash. I will rotary till, use plenty of fertilizer, irrigate four times, and spray three times. I expect around 1,600 jin per mu.

I do not chase the highest yields with the most fertilizer. At my age, I know that steady and moderate is better than gambling on something new. My neighbors who dump on extra nitrogen sometimes end up with lodging or just waste money. I will use what my land needs. I do rotary tillage for most crops; it is easier on me than deep ploughing, and the results are fine. My plan is practical, uses my well water wisely, and fits the labor I have. That is how I will manage.
